chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-A'mash, from Abaya ibn Rib'i, from Abdullah ibn Abbas. He said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Gabriel came to me and he was happy and joyful. So I said to him: My beloved Gabriel! Given your happiness, what is the status of my brother and cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib with his Lord? Gabriel said: O Muhammad! By Him who sent you with prophethood and chose you with messengership, I did not descend at this time except for this. O Muhammad, God the Most High, the Most Exalted, conveys His salaam to you and says: Muhammad is the prophet of My mercy, and Ali is the establisher of My proof. I shall not punish one who follows him even if he disobeys Me, nor shall I show mercy to one who opposes him even if he obeys Me.

Ibn Abbas said: Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, Gabriel (peace be upon him) will come to me holding the Banner of Praise in his hand. It consists of seventy strips, each of which is wider than the Sun and the Moon. He will give it to me, and I will take it and give it to Ali ibn Abi Talib. A man then said: O Messenger of Allah! How will Ali be able to carry the Banner when you said that it consists of seventy strips, each of which is wider than the Sun and the Moon?! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became angry and said: O man!

On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will give Ali strength like that of Gabriel (peace be upon him), beauty like that of Yusuf (peace be upon him), forbearance like that of Ridwan, and a voice resembling that of Dawud (peace be upon him). Had Dawud not been the reciter of Paradise, Ali would have been given a voice like his. Indeed, Ali will be the first to drink from the Salsabil and Zanjabil. And surely Ali and his Shi'a have a station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that the former and latter peoples will envy.

key_terms.الزَّنْجَبِيلُ: Zanjabil — ginger-flavored drink or spring in Paradise, mentioned in Quran 76:17
key_terms.السَّلْسَبِيلُ: Salsabil — a spring/river in Paradise mentioned in Quran 76:18
key_terms.شِيعَتِهِ: his Shi'a — his followers and partisans
key_terms.لِوَاءُ الْحَمْدِ: Banner of Praise — the eschatological banner carried on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.مُقِيمُ حُجَّتِي: Establisher of My proof — the one who upholds and manifests God's divine argument
key_terms.وَالَاهُ: followed him/gave allegiance to him — referring to wilaya (guardianship) of Ali

ai.seo_question: What did Gabriel tell the Prophet about the status of Ali ibn Abi Talib with God?
ai.summary: This hadith narrated from the Prophet through Ibn Abbas describes Gabriel descending to deliver God's divine testimony regarding Ali ibn Abi Talib's supreme status. God declares that Muhammad is the prophet of His mercy and Ali is the establisher of His proof, with extraordinary consequences: allegiance to Ali supersedes even disobedience to God, while enmity toward Ali nullifies even obedience. The Prophet further elaborates that on the Day of Resurrection, Ali will carry the Banner of Praise, be endowed with angelic strength, prophetic beauty, and paradisiacal voice, and will be first to drink from the rivers of Paradise — a position that will be envied by all of humanity.
